chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who carried food with another man in a ship, and it decreased, he (the Imam) said: 'He is liable (for the loss).' I said: 'Perhaps it increased.' He said: 'Do you know that it increased by something?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It is yours.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability for loss of goods shared between two partners during transport?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default presumption of liability (daman) in shared custody (qarad) scenarios, establishing that the custodian bears the risk of loss unless proven otherwise. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty regarding the cause of loss or gain places the burden of proof on the party retaining the benefit, ensuring fairness in commercial partnerships. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for determining liability in mixed-cause losses where the specific cause is unknown.
